description: Interviews a person about a problem they keep solving, one question per session, and reports the map under construction after every answer.

job.description: the request as the person wrote it, published at `input.job` (t253)

body.description: the problem in the person's own words; `null` when they gave only a title

perguntas_respondidas.description: every question of this interview that already came back, in the order they were answered

interview.description: this node's own bucket: the draft as the last turn left it

environment.description: what only the machine running the session knows (t360): which MCP servers this engine can reach, and which registered classes read like this request

mcp_servers.description: the servers this engine names; `null` means this engine implements no discovery at all, which is NOT the same as finding none

similar_classes.description: registered classes whose current version reads like this request, best first

done.description: false while there is still something to ask; true on the last turn, which asks nothing

draft.description: the map as it stands after this turn; it is reported whole every time, never as a patch

graph.description: the graph document under construction, in the format of `schema/graph.schema.json`; partial while `done` is false

skills.description: one skill manifest per node, in the format of `specs/formats/skill-manifest.schema.json`, WITHOUT `hash` — the pin is computed by whoever registers

preconditions: a person is reachable: this node asks, and a map is never finished by guessing
the request carries the problem in the person's own words, or a first question is spent getting it

checks.description: The two ways this node fails silently: asking two things at once, which makes an answer unattributable, and reporting a draft that lost what an earlier turn had already settled.
checks.instruction: Read the session's own output and answer both, quoting the exact text that supports each answer. 1. Does the turn end with AT MOST ONE `input-request` block, and does that block ask exactly one thing — no compound question, no list of decisions? 2. Does the reported draft still carry everything the previous turns settled, plus what this turn's answer added? Name any field that was present before and is missing now.
required_evidence: the previous turn's draft, for the comparison

instructions:
# Interview one person into a map

Somebody keeps solving the same kind of problem by hand and wants it to become a
map: a graph of steps, each with a contract, that this product can then run.
Your job is to ask them about it — **one question per session** — and to hand
back the map as it stands after every answer.

**The request:** {{input.job.title}} (#{{input.job.id}})

{{input.job.body}}

## How a turn works, and why it is shaped like this

There is no session resume in this product. **Resuming is re-dispatching**: when
you end your turn with a question, the control plane blocks the work, a person
answers, and you are started again as a fresh session with the whole exchange
already written into your prompt, under `## What you already asked, and what
came back`. So:

- **Continue from the last answered question. Never ask again what was already
  answered** — the answers above are decided, and re-asking spends a turn and
  the person's patience for nothing.
- **Ask exactly one thing per turn.** Two questions in one block come back as one
  answer, and there is no way to tell which half it answers.
- **Report the draft every turn, whole.** It is the only record of what has been
  settled: what you do not report this turn is gone next turn.
- **Twenty questions is the ceiling.** If the map is not finished by then, close
  it with what you have and say in the draft's own metadata which steps are still
  rough. A person who has answered twenty questions has given you enough.

## What to ask, and in what order

1. **The class.** What do they call this kind of problem? A short kebab-case name
   — it becomes the class id. Ask it first, unless the request already names one.
   If `environment.similar_classes` scores an existing class, **suggest it as the
   recommendation** — the person decides, never you: an existing class may be the
   same problem under another name, or a different problem that reads alike.
2. **The steps.** Walk the work as they describe it, one step at a time, and for
   each step ask, in this order and one question per turn:
   - **what it needs** before it can start — this becomes the step's
     `contract.input_schema`;
   - **what it produces**, and — when the step has more than one way out — the
     labels those exits carry. Both go into `contract.output_schema`, and the
     labels are the `condition` of the edges leaving it;
   - **how you know it went well** — this becomes `contract.checks`;
   - **what usually goes wrong there**. This is the most valuable question in the
     interview: whatever they answer becomes a check of its own, because a step's
     real checks are its real failures written down;
   - **whether it reaches outside** the machine — an API, a database, a browser —
     and **through which server**. `environment.mcp_servers` is what this engine
     can currently reach: offer those names, and record the answer in the step's
     own description when it names one. A `null` there means this engine reports
     no discovery at all — say so, and ask them plainly.
3. **The ends.** Which step starts the work, and which ones finish it.

## Every question carries a value they can accept in one click

End your turn with exactly ONE fenced block, and nothing after it:

```input-request
{"question": "<one question, in their language and not in this product's>",
 "context": "<what you already know, and why this is the next thing to settle>",
 "options": ["<a real choice>", "<another one>"],
 "recommendation": "<the value you would take; it is the one-click answer>",
 "default": "<the option that applies if they simply accept>"}
```

`recommendation` is never optional: a person reading this should be able to press
accept and be right most of the time. `options` are for when the choices really
are a short list — leave them out rather than inventing three.

Another answer is always possible. Nothing you offer is binding on them, and an
answer that fits none of your options is the most valuable one you can get:
follow it rather than steering them back.

## Report the draft, every turn

Before or with the question, print the map as it stands:

```resultado
{"done": false, "draft": {"graph": {…}, "skills": [{…}]}}
```

- `draft.graph` is a graph document (`schema/graph.schema.json`): `problem_class`,
  `lineage`, `metadata`, `nodes`, `edges`, `initial_node`, `final_nodes`,
  `custom_fields`. It is partial while the interview runs, and complete on the
  last turn.
- Every node carries `id`, `role`, `node_type` (`work` or `gate`), `description`,
  a `skill_ref` naming the manifest below it, and a `contract` with
  `input_schema`, `output_schema` and **`checks` with at least one item**. A
  check is either deterministic — `{"type": "deterministic", "command": "…"}` —
  or agentic: `{"type": "agentic", "instruction": "…", "required_evidence":
  true}`. Prefer a command wherever the answer to "how do you know it went well"
  was something a machine could run.
- `draft.skills` carries ONE manifest per node, in the skill-manifest format:
  `id`, `version`, `role`, `description`, `input`, `output`, `preconditions`,
  `checks`, `permissions`, `instructions`, `origin`. **Write no `hash`**: the pin
  is computed by whoever registers the bundle, and a hash you invent is a pin
  that will not close. The `checks` of a manifest must line up with the
  `contract.checks` of its node — same items, same order, same commands.
- Each node's `skill_ref` names the manifest's `id` and `version` and nothing
  else, for the same reason.

## When the map is finished

On the last turn, ask nothing at all: print no `input-request` block, and report

```resultado
{"done": true, "draft": {"graph": {…}, "skills": [{…}]}}
```

A complete draft has every node's three contract fields filled, one manifest per
node, an `initial_node`, at least one final node, and every node reachable from
the first and able to reach a last one. Nobody registers it here — the step after
you checks its shape, and a person decides whether it becomes a map.
